facts.fact: A The Conversation analysis of September 2025 says South African statutes cover deepfake harms: the Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020 criminalises electronic publication of intimate images without consent, and the Electoral Act 73 of 1998 bans publishing false information to influence elections.
facts.system: Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020; Electoral Act 73 of 1998

ZAF.note: No government use of AI is stated.
No AI tool in a sector system is stated.
No AI model, dataset or computing built in South Africa is stated.

facts.fact: A The Conversation analysis of September 2025 cites the Cybercrimes Act 19 of 2020 as a law that criminalises electronic publication of intimate private images without consent.
A The Conversation analysis of September 2025 cites the Protection of Personal Information Act as prohibiting misuse of personal information that infringes privacy.

ZAF.note: The article states nothing on criticism of government, punishment for speech or internet cuts.
The South African Police Service is mentioned only as hard-pressed to trace deepfake perpetrators; no station record system is stated.
